title.narrative: Valuing Nature and Nature-based Solutions for Sustainable Blue and Green Pathways for the Tourism, Food and Urban Sectors in Saint Lucia

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The private sector will be a key partner in the development of programs that incentivize businesses that depend on or support the tourism sector to adopt sustainable practices incorporating NbS. The Saint Lucia Hospitality & Tourism Association as the umbrella organization representing the hospitality sector will be the lead entity for consultation. They will be an important partner with government in the development of targeted tax incentives for environmentally responsible businesses. Noting that any tax concessions targeted to private sector enterprises should actively contribute to environmental conservation and not lead to perverse social and environmental outcomes. These subsidies should be carefully designed to ensure equitable distribution of benefits to all stakeholders. This would require clearly defined criteria for eligibility, such as adopting eco-friendly practices, reducing carbon footprint, and supporting local communities. Another important private sector partner will be the insurance industry, represented by the Insurance Council of St. Lucia. By leveraging the expertise of this body, this project can enhance NbS resilience to climate-related challenges, ensuring the long-term success of environmental conservation efforts. This type of collaboration also facilitates the alignment of financial instruments with climate goals, contributing to broader sustainability objectives. The banking and loan provision sector (including credit unions), represented by the Bankers Association of Saint Lucia (BASL) and the St. Lucia Co-operative Credit Union League have a similar role to play including providing bridging financing that allows for the implementation of sustainability into industry practices in these sectors (tourism, agriculture and urban). Overall, the focus on the private sector within these incentives aims to engage businesses in sustainable practices, aligning economic interests with environmental conservation. By providing financial incentives and building capacity, the private sector can play a crucial role in promoting responsible tourism and contributing to the success of the project in St. Lucia.
